The two kings are the Sun and the Moon; the leader is Mars; the prince is Mercury; the poet and the priest are Jupiter and Venus; the minister is Saturn; and the servant is considered so by the best of astrologers.
Copper, white, red, green, yellow, variegated, and black are the colors of the Sun; while dark blue, pale yellow, tawny, and golden are the colors of the Moon, the Lord of Śacī.

The Sun, Venus, Mars, Rāhu, Saturn, the Moon, Jupiter, and Mercury are the lords of the directions. The waning Moon, Saturn, Mars, and Rāhu are malefic planets; Mercury is also malefic when conjoined with a malefic planet.
Mercury and the Sun are considered neuter; Venus and the Moon are females; the remaining planets are recorded as males.
Mars and the others are known to dwell in fire, earth, milk, and water, respectively.

The poet and the priest are Mars and the Sun; Jupiter is the protector of the Vedas; Mercury is the protector of the castes in order; Saturn is declared the lord of the outcastes, and likewise Rāhu is the lord of the Mlecchas.

The Moon, Sun, Jupiter, Mercury, Venus, Mars, and Saturn are the [lords of] the *sāttvika* and other [qualities]. The deities are Indra, the Moon, Agni, Yama, Nirṛti, Varuṇa, Vāyu, Kubera, Īśvara, and Brahmā. NarP_1,55.20 //
A garment, dry land, something new, that which is struck by fire, a giver of liquor, as well as something cracked, copper scorched by the sun, silver, and likewise brass; NarP_1,55.21.
Gold, bell-metal, and iron are proclaimed as the [three] components for the [planets] beginning with Śiśira (Mercury),
respectively, when the Sun, Venus, Mars, the Moon, Mercury, and Jupiter are rising.

O Nārada, Saturn, Jupiter, Mars, and the others [Mercury and Venus] respectively aspect the third, eleventh, tenth, eighth, seventh, and the other [the fourth] houses, increasing in strength as they do so. When they are full [in strength], they aspect in this sequence.
For the Sun, during the solstices, moments, days, seasons, months, half-months, and autumns, the tastes are respectively pungent, bitter, alkaline, mixed, sweet, sour, and astringent. (NarP 1.55.24)

From the trine [of Jupiter], these are respectively: the ninth lord (Sāntya), the fourth lord (Dharma), the tenth lord (Āyuḥ), the eleventh lord (Sukha), the Sun (Khodyapa), a friend (Suhṛt), Jupiter (Jīva), Jupiter and Mercury (Jīvajñau), Venus and Mercury (Sitajñau), the Sun and Moon (Vyarkā), and Mars and the Sun (Vyārāḥ). NarP_1,55.25 //
Venus, the Sun, Mars, Mercury, and the Moon are friends to one another; the others are held to be neutral.
Mutual friendship exists between the second, twelfth, eleventh, third, and fifth houses, as well as the tenth and fourth. 55.26.
O Sage, having understood the devotees of Dhyeka through me, one should again designate Miśrīdīta along with the Sahajas, preceded by my Kāla, Udhi, Suhṛt, and Mitra.
The strength arising from position is determined by the planets being in their own signs, exaltations, or triplicities, as well as by the degrees of the *praṇava* (nine) divisions;
[the directions are assigned] to Mercury and Jupiter in the east, the Sun and Mars in the south, Saturn in the west, and Venus and the Moon in the north.
Others,
however, say that at the conjunction [of the planets], those situated in the north, having bright rays, and being active, are considered to be endowed with strength.
Saturn, Mars, and the Moon are always [strong] at night, while the others are strong during the day;
the malefics are strong in the dark fortnight and the benefics in the bright fortnight—this is considered by the wise to be the strength of time.
There is a mutual preponderance of Saturn, Mars, Jupiter, Venus, the Moon, and the Sun;
however, the malefic planets are strong while the benefics are weak when situated in the *kaṇṭaka* houses.
If it is a neuter [ascendant], the birth is equal to the portions of Venus, or even of the Moon and Sun;
if malefics are in their own divisions and benefics are situated in the divisions of others, the birth is from a non-womb (viyonija).
When it is weak, the birth from a wrong passage (viyoni) should be declared by the learned;
likewise, the head, the crooked neck, the feet, the shoulders, the back, and the chest [are to be noted].
The sides, the flanks, the anus, the feet, the penis, the testicles, and likewise the buttocks,
and the tail— these are known as the zodiac signs, beginning with Aries, among the limbs of four-footed animals.
One should declare the castes from the planet endowed with strength as seen from the ascendant's navamsha;
and the proportions [of the castes] should be determined by the measure of the aspect, while a line is drawn for the desired [caste] based on those situated in the Smara (seventh) house.
When the third part of the sky (the air element) possesses the fire of strength, and the final part is joined by a planet, there are land-lotuses;
when the twelfth part is joined by Saturn, O twice-born ones, they arise from the yoga of observation.
One should declare the birth of trees from the Moon, Jupiter, and the Sun;
for the others, it is stated that they arise from land, water, and dung.
The lord of the sign [occupied by] a planet from the ascendant, in whichever house it may be,
determines that many [planets] as land-born or water-born respectively.
Under the Sun and Saturn, trees have inner sap; under the Moon, they are unfortunate;
under Mars, they are thorny; under Jupiter and Mercury, they possess both fruit and flowers.
A planet is glossy when in conjunction with Venus, blooming when with the Moon, and bitter when with Mars;
likewise, it is auspicious when in an inauspicious asterism, and it makes even an auspicious tree grow on poor soil.
Or, moving in reverse order, one should perform it equally with the [planets] occupying their own signs or those mentioned as transiting others;
thus, for women here, the monthly menses are caused by Mars and the Moon. 55.41.

If Jupiter is situated in the seventh house, or otherwise located elsewhere while being aspected by a malefic planet joined with a woman, and if the eighth house is occupied or aspected by malefics, there is anger; however, if it is aspected by benefic planets, there is affection.
O best of Brahmins, when Venus, the Sun, and Mercury occupy their own signs and Jupiter is situated in an angle or a trine,
children endowed with excellent vigor shall be born to men.
If Mars and Saturn are in the seventh house, they bring disease to the man and woman;
however, if they are joined with or aspected by a planet in the twelfth house, they bestow dance upon them both.
Venus and the Sun are the mother and father; the Moon and Mars are so by night and day respectively.
The two known as the maternal aunt and the paternal uncle are auspicious when situated in even signs, like lotuses in a pond.
If a benefic planet is in an evil aspect, or is waned, or situated in its exaltation sign while occupying the ascendant,
and is gazed upon by a waned Moon and Mars, those who have gone there will certainly meet their death.
When the ascendant and the moon are situated either simultaneously or separately between malefic planets,
then a woman who is pregnant shall meet her death.
If malefic planets are situated in the fourth house from both the ascendant and the Moon, and Mars is in the eighth house,
while the Moon is waned (in conjunction with the Sun), and the Sun and Mars are in the sixth and eighth houses respectively, death occurs.
When Mars and Saturn are in the *tanu* (first) and *asta* (seventh) houses respectively, there is destruction caused by weapons;
one should abandon that month during which the lord of the month has perished, as it is a period of outflow (*saṃsrava*).
If the benefic planets are situated in the ascendant, the Moon, the third, eleventh, seventh, fourth, or tenth houses, while the malefic planets are in the third, sixth, or eleventh houses,
and the fetus is aspected by the Sun, it will be healthy.

When the Sun, Jupiter, the Moon, and the Ascendant are endowed with strength in the Ojah houses, or when Jupiter and Mars are situated in odd-numbered houses, one should then declare that it is a male birth.
When Venus, the Moon, and Venus are situated in even signs and have reached the positions of the watches (yāma),
the wise should declare the birth of a woman.
Occupying two houses and aspected by Mercury, they adorn their own side;
likewise, Saturn situated in the seventh house from the ascendant produces a multitude of offspring.
If the Moon and Jupiter, or Mars and Saturn, aspect each other, the Sun is even; however, if they are situated in odd or even signs respectively, the Moon is retrograde. ||| NarP_1,55.54 |||
If Mars aspects [the lord of the ascendant], it is a male; if it is a neuter sign, it is a daughter; if it is an even sign, it is a hermaphrodite.
Venus and the Moon in an odd sign, or Mercury, Mars, Jupiter, and Saturn aspected by a male planet, produce a son.

When the Moon and Jupiter are together in the ascendant or in the second house, or when the planets occupying the ascendant aspect the degrees of the body-parts in their own signs, [the native will possess those parts]. (NarP 1.55.56)
One should predict the three [results] as equal through unmixed [planets], starting from the portion of knowledge;
and when the ascendant is situated in the final degrees of Sagittarius, by means of the strong planets occupying those same degrees.
Those who possess the Sun and Mercury as lords of the second and fifth houses, respectively, and are aspected by Mars and Jupiter, are wealthy and possessors of many vehicles.
Venus, Mars, Jupiter, the Sun, the Moon, Saturn, Mercury, the lord of the ascendant, the Sun, and the Moon are the lords [of the signs].
The auspicious and inauspicious [results] for one who has entered the womb should be declared for the same number of months;
when Mercury is in the third house and the others are destroyed, he is endowed with two faces, daily meals, and a wife.
When the junctions [of the lunar mansions] are occupied by inauspicious planets, one is born speechless, deaf, and dull-witted;
and when the junctions are conjoined with the eight planets and the sun, one becomes a hero accompanied by songs.
If Mars and Saturn occupy the portion of the sign of sacrifice (the ninth house), then the fetus is born with teeth;
if it is in a goat-sign (Aries or Capricorn) and aspected by Mars and Saturn, the one in the womb is a hunchback;
if it is in a ram-sign (Aries) or a fish-sign (Pisces), and aspected by the lords of the angles (the ascendant and the tenth house), or situated at the junction of the limbs and the belly.
If the Moon is conjoined with malefic planets and devoid of the aspect of benefics, the fetus is dull-witted;
if it is situated in the twelfth or the last (twelfth) house and aspected by Saturn and the Sun, the child is a dwarf.

By the third-parts (trīṃśāṃśas) of Mercury, Jupiter, and Venus, respectively, there are those who are wise, wealthy, and beautiful; by those same planets being in malefic [third-parts], there are those who are bald-headed and deformed.
If Leo is joined by the Sun and Moon and aspected by Mars and Saturn, one is born blind;
if aspected by mixed planets, one has eyes like bubbles.
If the Sun is in the twelfth house from Jupiter, he destroys the right eye. (NarP 1.55.63)
Yogas aspected by benefics are not desired; they would be malefic, of this there is no doubt.
If Saturn is in its sign of debilitation, in its own Navāṃśa, or in its Mūlatrikoṇa, birth occurs within three years.
In the same manner, one should also consider the sons when the Moon is in the twelfth house.
The malefics are twelve degrees from the moon at the time of conception, situated ahead of it in those same signs.
In the case of the Moon, the desired minutes [of arc] are known to be double the degrees of the birth-portion and so forth.
The birth may occur in the absence of the father when the moon does not aspect the ascendant.
When the Sun has fallen from the middle [of the zodiac] and is situated in a foreign land at birth, there is indeed no birth of an enemy;
likewise when Saturn is in the body [the first house], Mars and the Sun are present, and Mercury and Venus are situated in the middle, while the Moon is in the ascendant.
When three parts of the lotus of the wicked limb, or two, are occupied by auspicious planets,
the Sun is known by the best of astrologers to have risen, or else to be visible in that aspect.
O best of sages, when the sun is situated in a quadruped asterism and the planets are endowed with the remaining strengths, twins are born from the womb.

When Jupiter does not aspect the ascendant, the Moon, or the Sun and Moon together, while being situated in the sign of the woman’s natal asterism or at a degree equal to her natal asterism, [the child will be female]. (NarP 1.55.72)
If the Sun is in a sign with malefics, the native will either be born of another's seed or cause the procreation of another's offspring;
likewise, if the two [ascendant and seventh] signs are occupied by malefic planets and situated in the Sun’s quadrants, sextiles, or trines.

If the father is abroad, aged, or afflicted by disease due to the influence of the zodiacal sign at the time of the query, he will survive if the Moon is full, Jupiter is in its own sign, and a benefic planet is situated in the first house.
O Nārada, when the Moon has entered the eighth house, a woman gives birth to a daughter; or if the Moon is full and aspects the fourth, seventh, or tenth house, she likewise bears a female child.

If Saturn is in its own strength and situated in the ascendant at birth, there is no doubt that the delivery occurs in water; if it is aspected by malefics and positioned in the eighth, first, fourth, or twelfth house from the ascendant, the birth is in the private parts.
When Venus is in the ascendant of Cancer and is aspected by Jupiter and the Moon,
or when Saturn is in the natal ascendant and is aspected by Mercury, the Sun, and the Moon.
Birth occurs respectively in a place of play, a temple, or a desert;
[if the Moon and Venus are] in the ascendant, in a cremation ground, or in a blood-stained rural location.
If Mercury is born in the house of the Agnihotra fire, in a house adorned with ornaments,
or in a workshop, he will be endowed with strength.
When the Moon is situated in its own sign, its own division, or its own house,
or when it occupies a trine from Mars or Saturn, or when those two are set, the child is brought forth by the mother.
If Jupiter aspects it, however, one attains long life and even more;
but if Saturn aspects the ascendant and Mars is in the seventh house, one perishes.
If Mars and Saturn are seen together in the ninth house, one is happy though fallen into the hands of others;
it is a month of misfortune for life, even with fellow travelers.

O Sage, birth occurs in the house of the father or mother according to the strength of its lord; the ascendant and the moon are not situated together in a tree-house, nor in an auspicious sign, nor in their depression, nor in mutual aspect.
Then, endowed with these characteristics,
there is confidence in a secluded place when the Moon is in the portion of Saturn's asterism in the fourth house, aspected by Saturn, or even by Jupiter.
One should likewise predict birth during a period of poor worship, in darkness, on low ground, with the head [down], or when the back is turned toward the rising [sun]. (NarP 1.55.85)
If the Moon is situated in the eighth house from the ascendant along with malefic planets, one should predict suffering for the mother;
if Saturn is there, the house will be dilapidated or rebuilt, but if the Moon is there, it will be burnt or not at all.
A house that is rich in wood but not firm is for Mercury; one endowed with many crafts is for Mercury; one decorated with paintings is for Venus; and a firm and beautiful new house is for Jupiter.
In Aquarius, Aries, Leo, and Aquarius, the residence is in the east;
in Gemini and Virgo, it is indeed in the north; in Taurus, it is in the west; and in Capricorn and Leo, the residence shall be in the south.

In the house, two [deities] each are located in the east and other cardinal directions; the goat and others occupy the corners with two limbs each; on the side-frames are the feet like those of Vāstu; and the final signs of the zodiac are situated in the corners with six limbs each.
Those planets situated within the interior of the moon's orb are declared to be "sūtikās" (producers);
indeed, according to whether they are seen or unseen from outside or inside the circle, they are otherwise [classified].
The planet situated in the same sign as the Lagna,

the Moon, or the Sun, or even in the same Navamsha as the Moon or the Sun, possesses a complexion corresponding to that [of the luminaries] and is endowed with the respective bodily parts beginning with the head.
The head, the ears, the nose, the cheeks, the jaws, and the mouth;
the throat, the shoulders, the sides, the heart, the back, the chest, the navel, and the anus are the *vāstika* (vital points).
One should state that the penis falls upon the testicles, the buttocks, and likewise the knees; and both the shanks and the feet [fall] upon both [sides] by means of the combined three parts.

If [a planet] is conjoined with a malefic, there is a wound on that limb; if it is conjoined with that same [planet], there is a mark. However, if it is in its own sign or division and conjoined with a fixed sign, the mark is innate; otherwise, it is adventitious.
In the case of Mercury, injury arises from wind or stones; in that of Mars, it is born of poison, weapons, or fire;
in that of Jupiter, it is caused by wood or animals; and for the victor [Saturn], it originates from horns or from being struck down.

In whichever limb the three planets associated with the [relevant] sign are situated, there certainly occurs a wound caused by something inauspicious, provided that [the lord of the sign] is located in the back part of the body corresponding to that sign.
One born under the Sun is a maker of *tilaka* marks, possesses wealth, is endowed with eight gentle qualities,
has a square face, tawny eyes, is of bilious temperament (*paittika*), and has sparse hair.
One born under the Moon is wise, possesses wind and phlegm, is slow of speech, and has auspicious eyes;
one born under Mars is fierce-eyed, youthful, bilious, and likewise fickle.
One who has three folds [on the belly], who knows how to laugh and what is pleasing, and whose speech is coherent;
one who is tawny, smooth-skinned, tall, phlegmatic, wise, and venerable—such a person is considered a Piṅgaka.
Suvapu, Locana, Kṛṣṇavakrakeśa, Bhṛgu, Sukhī,
Dīrgha, Kapiladṛḍhabandha, and Nīlīkharakacolasa.

The bodily constituents (dhātus) are sinew, bone, blood, skin, semen, fat, and marrow; they correspond respectively to Mars, the Sun, the Moon, Mercury, Venus, Jupiter, Saturn, and the Earth. (NarP 1.55.101)

Death occurs in the sign of Cancer (Kīṭa) when there are malefic planets in the angles from the Moon, with malefics in the fourth house, and both malefics and benefics in the first and seventh houses.
If both malefic planets are situated at the ascendant and the seventh house, and the Moon is not aspected by any benefic joined with a malefic, then the death of the born person will certainly occur.

If the Moon is waned and situated in the twelfth house, and malefic planets occupy the ascendant and the eighth house while no benefics are present, or if the Moon is conjoined with Mars and occupies a quadrant, the seventh, the twelfth, the eighth, or the ascendant; [then death occurs].
If the lord of the ascendant and others are not aspected by Saturn, they bestow death;
likewise, if they are not aspected by Saturn in the sixth, eighth, or twelfth house, death occurs immediately, unless they are aspected by benefics.
If the eighth house is conjoined with or aspected by mixed planets, there is death for the infant;
likewise, if a malefic planet is situated in the eighth, the ascendant, or the fourth house, and is positioned between two other malefics.
If the eighth house from the Moon is devoid of planets, or likewise if it is so from the Ascendant, there is death for the infant;
provided that malefic planets occupy the seventh house from the Moon, without the presence of a mutual aspect between them.

If the Moon is in a benefic sign and situated in the eleventh house, and malefics are placed in the trines or the seventh house; or if the Moon is with malefics in the fourth house, or if it is situated in the seventh house with malefics, one shall meet death.
If the lotus [the ascendant] is swallowed by malefics situated in the eighth house, death occurs from fire or from one's own son;
however, if the Sun is in the ascendant with strength and malefics go to the eighth, death is by a weapon.
When the Ascendant is joined by Saturn, the Moon, and Jupiter, and Venus is in a quadrant along with Mercury,
Saturn, and Mars occupying the third, sixth, and eleventh houses, an immeasurable lifespan certainly results.
When the supreme Varṇa is in Pisces as the ascendant, and the Moon is in Taurus seeking the principles (tattvas),
and all [planets] are situated in their own exaltations, the maximum lifespan is proclaimed.
If seen by benefics and endowed with strength while situated in a quadrant, it bestows longevity and wealth;

likewise when the lord of the ascendant is strong in its own sign, its own house, or its own exaltation, and the benefic planets are in their own signs or their own houses within the body [the ascendant].
Seventy years [are attained] when there is an auspicious planet in the kendras during the sixty-year cycle, and Jupiter is in its exaltation;
or when Jupiter is conjoined with benefics situated in their own signs or their Mūlatrikoṇas.
If the lord of the ascendant is endowed with strength, a lifespan of eighty years is declared;
if it possesses vigor while the benefic planets are in the quadrants (kendras), and the eighth house is cleared of malefics, [the span is] thirty years.
When the lord of the ascendant is in the ninth house and Jupiter is in the eighth, and they are aspected by malefic planets,
the lords of the ascendant and the eighth house, situated in the eighth house, are considered to bestow the lifespan of a year.
If the Ascendant is occupied by malefic planets and Jupiter is aspected by Saturn, there will be some physical deformity;
if Rāhu and Saturn are situated in the ninth or tenth house, and Venus is in a quadrant while the Moon is in the twelfth or ninth house [the same result follows].
If Jupiter is in Cancer, Venus and Jupiter are situated in the tenth house, and the lord of the eighth house is devoid of benefic planets in the ascendant, the lifespan is one hundred years.
If [the lord of the eighth] is in the eighth house, the lifespan is eighty-four years.
If the lord of the eighth house is in the ascendant and the lord of the ascendant is in the eighth house, the lifespan is five years;
if there is a conjunction of Venus and Jupiter, or if Mercury and the Moon are in the ascendant and Saturn is in the eighth house, the lifespan is five years.
This shall be the lifespan produced by yoga; now the clear [calculation] is set forth:
the *paiṇḍa* [lifespan] is used when the Sun has greater strength, and that from nature (*nisarga*) when the Moon has greater strength.
If the ascendant is strong, its portion of the lifespan is as follows; now hear the method for calculating that:
six, twenty-one, twenty-five, fifteen, fifteen, twenty-one, fifteen, fifteen, and twenty, respectively. (NarP 1.55.120)
The nails, the moon, the two hooks, the steadfastness, the eyes, the sky, and the arrows.
When, in the aggregate (piṇḍa) at birth, the Sun is in its exaltation and no planet is less than six degrees [in excess],
then it is considered that the degrees remaining after subtracting the zodiacal circle (cakraśuddha) are to be accepted as the life span.
In both the *śatru* and *ubha* [divisions], the degrees should be reduced by one-quarter, except for a planet in retrograde motion;
and in the *manda* and *śukti* divisions, they should be reduced by half, as well as for a planet that has set.
When a malefic planet is in the ascendant, one should add [the degrees] to the two losses;
then, excluding the enemy [planets], one should multiply the degrees and so forth by the [remaining] factors and divide by the [lunar] days. (NarP 1.55.124)

These [degrees] should be diminished by the degrees of the asterism (bhagaṇa) obtained; for a malefic planet, the degrees should be increased by half and then decreased by half, while for a benefic planet, they should be decreased by half. NarP_1,55.125 //
Those clear degrees, multiplied by sixty (kha-ṣaṭ-tri), are [the years] by their respective multipliers;
the remainder, multiplied by twelve (arka), divided by the divisor, is known as the months.
The remainder of that, multiplied by three and divided by that same [divisor], yields the days;
and when the remainder is multiplied by sixty and divided by the divisor, it gives the ghaṭīs and so forth.
Having subtracted the portions of the *bhājya* and other parts and reduced them to fractional form, one should divide by sixty (the "eyes of the sky");
as for the remainder, however, it should be multiplied by twelve and so forth.
The lifespan of the Moon, the Ascendant, and the other planets, including their signs, is clearly produced by dividing [the degrees] by fourteen;
the degrees of the planets, together with the Ascendant, are then divided to determine the years of life.
The years multiplied by four shall be the degrees of the lifespan; I shall now describe the correction for that to you:
if the planet and the ascendant are six signs apart, there is a correction, otherwise there is none.
The quotient obtained by dividing that part by its own fire (three) shall be subtracted from the earth;
when there is unity, then the parts of the asterism (nakṣatra) and the earth multiplied by the quotient of its own maximum (twenty-seven) shall be subtracted.
It is certain that half of the sin belongs to the one who officiates at the sacrifice, while the whole belongs to the one who performs it;
and for those who kill a preceptor, the portions of their lifespan [are lost]—this is declared to be the purification.

The lifespan, divided by the degrees and minutes [of the ascendant], multiplied by twenty years, and then divided by two hundred, yields the months; the remainder represents the days and so forth. (NarP 1.55.133)
The degrees of the ascendant's lifespan multiplied by three and divided by ten shall be the years;
from the remainder, when multiplied by twelve and divided by ten, the months and so forth shall be obtained.
The corrected lifespan shall be obtained by adding [the years] equal to the number of signs from the weaker limb;
the degrees of the ascendant are divided by two, and the months are derived from multiplying [the remainder] by thirty.
The remaining [periods], such as days and so forth, should be added; this does not apply to the *piṇḍa* and *nisarga* [systems].
However, between the Ascendant, the Sun, and the Moon, whichever is strongest, its *daśā* comes first.
Then, for those situated in the angles (kendras) and so forth, when there are two, three, or more planets, and for one who is strong;
he who has a long life and whose strength is equal to that of the Sun and others, is the first petitioner. NarP_1,55.137 //

[The planet] situated in a trine from the sixth house (ṣaḍvarga) or in the seventh house (smara), and [the one] situated in a square from the seventh house (saptama) or the fourth house (turya). // NarP_1,55.138 //

In this case as well, the sequence begins with the angles (kendras) and so forth; for a strong planet in the second, third, and other houses, the years are four, eight, and seven, while for one in the seventh house, they are four.
For a planet situated in a trine, or in the eighth house, or in the twelfth house,
or in the fourth or eighth house, the multipliers are proclaimed to be eight, two, twelve, and four, respectively.
O Nārada, [the results] are multiplied by ten, divided by the sum of the [planetary] strengths,
and then added to the remainder when the [longitude of the] Sun and others are multiplied by twelve and divided by the sum of the months and so forth.

Within the sub-periods (antardaśās), there are further sub-sub-periods (vidaśās) and likewise minor sub-periods (upadaśās); these are determined by whether the lord of the period is situated in a friend’s sign, its exaltation, its own sign, a quadrant, a trine, the second house, the fourth house, the seventh house, the eleventh house, or the third house.
That which is auspicious is the *bhaga* (fortune) when situated in the first house and so forth;
it is declared to be the cause of the destruction of those respective houses when situated in other positions.
Whatever substance belongs to a bird in the house of its disposition (bhāva) arising from the conjunction of moments (kṣaṇayoga),
one should apply all such results concerning livelihood and so forth to its respective period (daśā).
That planet which, when seen by an enemy [planet], causes misfortune during a state of adversity,
yet becomes auspicious when aspected by a benefic, and is situated within a favorable group (sadvarga), [is considered beneficial].
At that time, the powerful Āpanna-Āśakṛt is proclaimed;
moreover, its fruit arising from the eightfold group shall be entirely auspicious.
And for one who is emaciated in body and form, yet has attained growth and is situated in its own exaltation sign,
or in its own trine or a friendly sign, the result is middling and auspicious.
However, for one who has gone astray, one should speak what is most excellent or most auspicious;
knowing his strength, one should speak what is not harsh, even if it is unpleasant, but rather what is mild.
In the case of *aṅgabhaṅga* (bodily fracture), [the result] is from the [navamśa] that is good, middling, or evil; in the opposite case, it is from the stable [navamśa].
Furthermore, for a fixed sign, the result is derived from the third parts (*tryaṃśaka*) of the *horā*, starting from the last, the middle, and the first.
A *horā* joined with or aspected by its own lord, the sacrificer, or Jupiter brings good fortune;
however, it is otherwise if it is conjoined with or aspected by malefics or situated between malefics.
If the Sun is in the seventh house from its own sign, from Mars, or from Saturn, crows first appear for the death of relatives;
however, if it is six signs away from Venus, it pertains to the death of one's wife.

Those who meditate on the Dharma and those who know the three principles beginning with the individual soul (jīva) become wise; from that, those who have studied the sacred texts and are free from kinsmen will increase in excellence.
From the increase of the Gōng constellation, there is wealth, learning, and austerity; from Svār, the Moon is auspicious.
From Pṛthā, when it has reached its own increase, there are six and eight [years] for those approaching the five [periods].
If Jupiter is situated in the sixth, third, or eleventh house from Mercury, or occupies the second, third, eleventh, eighth, or a quadrant;
or if Venus is in a quadrant, the eighth, the eleventh, or the twelfth house from Jupiter, or in its own sign from Mercury; [then there is auspiciousness]. (Narapati-jayacaryā 1.55.154)
From the Moon, Mars is in the eighth house;
Mercury is in the fourth; Jupiter is in the tenth; Venus is in the seventh; Saturn is in the first from its own sign; and Rāhu is in the eighth from its own sign. (NarP 1.55.155)

Mars is auspicious when situated in the sixth, third, eleventh, or tenth house from Mercury; in the sixth, fifth, eighth, or twelfth house from Venus; and in the tenth, eleventh, second, or sixth house from Jupiter. 1,55.156.
In the sixth chapter of the Kavidhyā, Sañjñā [says]:
"When Saturn is in the third house from Jupiter, it directly causes birth, enmity, and death."

From the first, third, fifth, seventh, ninth, and eleventh houses from the ascendant (lagna), starting with the nature (svabhāva) of each, [the results] proceed through the six, ten, eight, four, three, and twelve [houses] respectively.
From the first house onwards, they are determined by the ascendant.
From Mars, Jupiter is located in the tenth, seventh, and third houses;
from the Sun, Saturn is in the third and eleventh; and from Venus, Mercury is in the tenth, fifth, and sixth houses.
From the Moon, [the houses] are 2, 9, 5, and 4; from Saturn, they are 5, 3, 6, and 12;
those which are 4, 4, 5, 6, 0, and 10 [from Jupiter]; and from Mercury, they are 2, 7, and 3, starting from the ascendant.
From the Sun (Sūrya) [the results] are swift in the eight houses; from the Moon (Candra), they are auspicious in the six;
from Mercury (Budha), in three; from Jupiter (Guru), in four; from Venus (Śukra), in ten; and from Saturn (Arka-ja), in nine.
In the case of the Sun, [the results] are in the ninth, twelfth, and tenth houses; for Jupiter, in the eighth, fourth, and tenth;
for Mercury, in the fourth, seventh, third, eleventh, sixth, second, and twelfth; and for Venus, in the third, sixth, second, and twelfth.
Mars is auspicious in the third, eleventh, and seventh houses from the ascendant;
Jupiter is auspicious in the tenth, fourth, and ninth; and the Sun is auspicious in the first, fourth, seventh, and tenth houses from the ascendant. || 163 ||
From Jupiter, [the results] are in the sixth, eighth, twelfth, and eleventh houses;
from Venus, in the second, third, sixth, and eleventh; and from Saturn, in the sixth, eighth, twelfth, and enemy (third) houses.
For those [planets] in the aforementioned positions, one should indeed draw lines; for those not mentioned, however, one should place dots.
As in the case of the birth sign, there is friendship, exaltation, and self-division [of aspects] toward others, while there is no aspect toward those who are enemies.

"Hardship, loss of wealth, and affliction; equanimity, attainment of wealth, and happiness; acquisition of riches, and the attainment of what is desired—such is the fruit of the lines in sequence. (NarP 1.55.166)

From one who hates his father, mother, friends, brothers, wife, or employees; from one who is hostile toward his master, the head of the village, or the king; and from one who, being healthy, seeks to differentiate himself from the sun or to destroy his own reputation.

One should predict one's livelihood from grass, gold, horses, and drivers during the portion of the Sun; from agriculture, lotuses, women, and water during the portion of the Moon; and from minerals, weapons, and daring deeds during the portion of Mars.

In the period of Venus, there is awakening through poetry, arts, and the like, as well as speed [of intellect] due to gods, Brahmins, and mines; whereas in the period of Saturn, it is indeed characterized by violence, toil, and base deeds.

Likewise, when Jupiter is in its own or exaltation sign, and the Moon is in a Navamsha of one, four, or seven, and is aspected by four or more planets, there will be kings among men. (Narapati-jayacharya 1.55.170)
If Mars is exalted in the second house, the Sun and Moon are in the tenth, and Jupiter is in the seventh, the fourth, the third, the first, or the tenth house, there will be twenty-two kings.
If Jupiter is in the sign of Aries, Leo, or Sagittarius while the Sun is exalted in the fourth house, there will be one king.

If Jupiter and the Moon are in the ascendant, Saturn and Mercury are in the sixth house, and Venus and Mars are in Libra, while Jupiter is in Cancer and the Sun is in the ascendant, there will be kings. (NarP 1.55.172)
If Jupiter and Saturn are in Taurus, Aries, or Cancer, and are situated in the houses of friends or the wife, one becomes a king;
likewise, if Saturn is in Capricorn, Aquarius, or Scorpio, and is situated in signs beginning with Aries, one becomes a king.
When Mars is in Capricorn with Sagittarius as its *tūṅga* (exaltation) portion, and Saturn is in Cancer as its *tūṅga* portion in the ascendant,
while Mercury, Jupiter, and Venus occupy the seventh house— NarP_1,55.174.
If the Sun is in Aries, Mars in Virgo, the Moon in Cancer, Saturn in Pisces,
and Jupiter in Leo, Aquarius, or Capricorn, the native becomes a king, provided the body [of the horoscope] is strong.

If the Sun and Jupiter are in the ascendant, one becomes a king; or if Mars and the Sun are situated in the fifth house, and Jupiter, the Moon, and Venus are on the earth (the first house), one is a king according to the wise. If Mercury is in the seventh house, one is a king.

If Saturn is in the sign of Capricorn (Mṛgaśīrṣa) and occupies the second, seventh, or tenth house from it, the king will be endowed with fame; likewise, if Venus and Mars occupy the seventh or tenth houses, he will become a renowned monarch.
O Lord of Sages, any man whose son is born under the aforementioned yogas shall become a king; furthermore, one whose son is born under the yogas to be described hereafter is to be known as a prince.
If the Sun is in its exaltation or in a trine division and is endowed with strength by Jupiter and the other planets, one becomes a king;
likewise when the Sun is in Leo with Aries as the ascendant, or when Mars is in Capricorn in the eighth house while the Moon is in Aquarius.
O Sage, if Venus is situated in its own sign, the Lord of the Earth shall be on the bow; likewise, if the Moon is in the eighth house and is conjoined with or aspected by benefics.
If the remaining planets occupy the three signs beginning with the ascendant, one is born as a lord of the earth;
provided that Mercury is situated in the ascendant, endowed with strength, powerful, and auspicious.
And with the remaining planets situated in the houses of Dharma (the ninth), Artha (the second), and Upacaya (the third, sixth, eighth, and eleventh), the king is endowed with righteousness.
When the Moon, Mercury, and Jupiter occupy the first, tenth, and fourth houses respectively, [the same result follows].
If Jupiter and Mars are in the second house and the Sun is in the fourth, then there is a king;
if Jupiter and the Sun are in the tenth house while Venus is in the seventh, the others [the remaining planets] are in the eleventh house.
In the fourth house, Jupiter, the Sun, Mars, and the Moon [are situated];

in the first house, Saturn, Rāhu, and Ketu; and in the seventh house, the hands [of the planets]. In the first house, Venus and Saturn, the Moon, Jupiter, Venus, the Sun, and Mercury are positioned in order.

They produce happiness and the attainment of auspicious positions and lordships; during the period (daśā) of the lord of the tenth house from the ascendant of the natal chart, there is association with royalty.
Or, during the period of a strong planet, planets situated in the sixth house, the sign of debilitation, or the directions of suffering cause distress;
whereas all planets occupying two adjacent angles (kendras) are said to bestow excellent divisions (vargas).
A bird [aspect] situated in the tenth house with planets occupying the third and seventh houses forms a *sakaṭa* (cart) yoga;

one situated in the ninth house with planets in the first and tenth houses forms a *śṛṅgāṭaka* (rhombus) yoga; and one situated in the ascendant with planets in the second and tenth houses is considered a *hala* (plow) yoga.

When the planets are situated in the Varja and Aṅga houses, they are considered "existent" (sat); when they are otherwise, they are "non-existent" (asat). When these are mixed, and when they occupy the fourth, tenth, or external houses, they are called "kamala," while those situated in the Vāyu and Kaṇṭaka houses are likewise described.

From the ascendant, with four [planets] in the eighth house, there is a sacrificial post; from the fourth, with four in the eighth, a spear; from the seventh, with four in the fifth, a trident; and from the tenth, with four in the first, a sword.

From the ascendant (lagna), the nokākūṭa is formed by seven degrees in successive order; from the eighth house (asta) it is called the umbrella (chatra); and from the second house (svabha), it is known as the half-moon (ardhendu). NarP_1,55.190 //

When the planets are situated one sign apart from the ascendant, there is a wheel; when they are in the sense-meaning of the lord of the ocean (the fourth house), there are lutes and such; and when they occupy equal and seventh signs, [there are other instruments].
The lute-string, the noose, the field, the ploughshare, the pair, and the ball—
when these signs occupy the divisions of the planets, it is proclaimed as a royal yoga (rājayoga).

When the benefics are situated in the angles from the ascendant and the second house, and the malefics are situated in the angles from the seventh house, Nala is said to be the Musala yoga named Sthirasthairya; when they are situated in the angles from the fourth house, it is called Sarpa.
One who desires sacrifice should move about; one intent on wealth should carry a pestle with a rope;
one who is deformed should be steady; one free from greed and pride should be silent; and one who has risen above the stain of sin should wear a garland of flowers.
Born from a lute, he is exceedingly skilled in song and dance, deeply fond of them;
he is a donor, prosperous, established in giving, born of a noose, and endowed with wealth and good character.

One born under Kṛttikā is a farmer; one born under Rohiṇī is a hero wounded by a spear; one born under Mṛgaśiras possesses wealth; one born under Ārdrā is a heretic; one born under Punarvasu is devoid of wealth and likewise impure.
With his feet worshipped by kings, endowed with royal enjoyments in the ocean,
possessing auspicious limbs, the half-moon [mark] on his chest, happy, and brave, he was a sovereign like a chowrie.
One born under the constellation Maitra becomes a benefactor, while one born under Kūṭa is a king who binds others with falsehood;
one born under Tautaja possesses fame and enjoys happiness; such a man certainly becomes virtuous.

One born under Tyāga is generous, a performer of sacrifices, and self-possessed; one under Yūtha is violent; one under Guhyādhipa is struck by arrows; one under Śakti is base and lazy; one under Daṇḍa is destitute and suffers separation from loved ones.

When the planets are situated in both the second and the twelfth houses from the Moon, excluding the Sun, there arise the *sunaphā*, *anaphā*, and *durudharā* yogas; otherwise, when the opposite occurs, it should be known as the *kemudruma* yoga.
One born in Sunaphā enjoys the wealth he has earned himself and is charitable, wealthy, and happy;
one born in Anaphā is free from disease, virtuous, famous, and well-attired.
If [the Moon] is in the *kema* tree, one becomes an enjoyer, happy, wealthy, generous, and a renouncer;
yet, born under a difficult burden, extremely impure, miserable, base, and then destitute.
When Mars is in the Puṣkara yoga, the person born is a maker of machines or stonework, a traveler, and very wise;
he is of good reputation, skillful, learned, and likewise wealthy.

O Sage, one who is devoted to mutual occupations, who lives by the trade of garlands and perfumes, who is dull-witted yet skilled in the elements, and likewise knows the art of carrying loads— NarP_1,55.204.
One should avoid false accusations, fraudulent merchandise, and selling blood, meat, or poison;
one should instead make oneself skilled in worldly affairs, humble, and endowed with good reputation.
O Sage, one born from Saturn and Jupiter is diligent, of unstable youth, noble-born, valiant, capable, and a knower of pleasure and pain.
Āre, Sajña, Vāhuyodhī, Purādhyakṣa, Sagīṣpati, Saśukra, Dyūtakraddheya, Nṛtī, Dyūti, and Samandaka. (NarP 1.55.207)
O Nārada, a man born when Jupiter is in the second house becomes rich, skilled in dance and song, and expert in illusion;
however, if Saturn is with Venus in that same house, he becomes a hunter and a cruel man.
When Jupiter is with Venus, one becomes learned; when with Saturn, one is a maker of food-pots;
when with Mercury, one possesses very little shame and relies on others for wealth.
When the planets are situated separately in the fourth and subsequent houses from the first, starting with four, five, six, seven, eight, nine, ten, and eleven respectively,
the man becomes a wandering mendicant— [in order] Mars, Mercury, Jupiter, Venus, Saturn, and the Sun.
One who lives as a Śākya, an Ājīvaka, an elder, or a seeker of wealth, or one who eats the fruits of the *arakha* tree,
shall suffer a fall from the religious life if he is expelled by their masters.

O Nārada, those who possess devotion to the deity situated there, even if they are uninitiated, have little merit, or are in a state of decline, will see [the deity] slowly if they are not seen by those born under other [planets] who are powerful and situated there.
If the Moon is in a weak birth-sign, or likewise in a weak Navāṃśa,
or in a portion of Mars or the Sun while aspected by Saturn, one becomes initiated [into the state of a mendicant].
One born under Aśvinī is handsome and adorned; under Yama (Bharaṇī), one is skillful and truthful in speech;
under Kṛttikā (Agni), one is a great eater; and likewise under Rohiṇī (Padā), one is firm-minded and pleasant of speech.

One born under Brāhma is wealthy; under Mṛga, one is an enjoyer of pleasures; under Raudra, one is violent, deceitful, and a doer of evil; under Ādityā, one is self-controlled yet diseased; under Puṣya, one is auspicious, a performer of sacrifices, wise, and happy.
In the *dhū* [digit] one becomes a rogue, a deceiver, ungrateful, and sinful; in the *ha* [digit], a devourer of all things.
In the *pa* [digit] one is an enjoyer; in the *tra* [digit], wealthy; in the *bha* [digit], devoted; in the *ga* [digit], a donor and one of pleasant speech.
In the constellation of Yama (Bharaṇī), a man is wealthy and enjoys pleasures; in Kṛttikā, he is a thief, audacious, and pitiless;
in Citrā, he wears variegated garments and possesses beautiful eyes; but in Viśākhā (Tvāṣṭra), he is not devoted to righteousness or compassion.
In Dvīśa, one is greedy, clever, angry, foolish, and travels abroad;
in Śakra, one is devoted to dharma, contented; and under Mūla, one is proud, wealthy, and happy.
In Āpya one is seen to be proud; in Vaiśva, humble and righteous;
in Karṇa, wealthy, happy, famous, generous, and brave; and in Vasu, wealthy.

In the Pauṣṇa asterism, one who is sickly becomes a slayer of enemies; one who is addicted to vice becomes a conqueror of women; one who is deceitful becomes a speaker at the base; one who is happy becomes beloved; and one who is brave becomes wealthy and pure.
One born in the Moon (Candra) is lustful, brave, grateful, unassailable, handsome, generous, and patient;
in Gemini, one is a womanizer, skilled in gambling and weapons, and devoted to women; in one's own sign (Cancer), one is short of stature. || 55.221 ||

In the sixth house, one is a hater of fortune, wrathful toward Hari, proud, valorous, steady-minded, happy, virtuous, gentle, wise, and learned; in the seventh house (the pitcher), one is tall and wealthy.

One born in Puṣya is a worshipful person; in Āśleṣā, one afflicted by injuries; in Maghā, a poet; in Pūrvaphalgunī, an artisan; in Uttaraphalgunī, wealthy; in Mṛgaśiras, lazy and wandering; in Citrā, handsome; and in Svātī, one who steals the wives and wealth of others.
If Mars is strong, there will be fear from elephants; if weak, the fruit is the opposite. This result is likewise for others [the remaining planets].
[The results of the lords of the houses are: [From the first house: famous, a hater of women, wealthy, sharp-witted, learned, a poet, a distiller of liquor, and wealthy.
When the Sun is in Aries or the following signs at birth, a person is worthy of honor, yet greedy and lacking friends who possess wealth.
If Mars is in the sign of Scorpio, one becomes wealthy; if it is in Cancer, one is a destroyer of one's own kin;
if in Taurus, one is grateful; if in Gemini, one is famous; and if in Virgo, one has another's wife. (NarP 1.55.225)
In Capricorn, one has many children and wealth; in Aquarius, one is miserable, untruthful, and wicked;
in Pisces, one is hated by women, hostile toward kinsmen, devoid of pleasure, and possessed of wisdom.

When Mercury is in the sign of the Sun or others, one who possesses wealth equal to his sons and wives and is free from debt becomes a commander of an army, enriched with women, wealth, and sons, and is capable, prosperous, and well-provided with attendants.
When Jupiter is in the sign of Leo, the lord of the mandala enjoys prosperity and happiness;
he is a master of gold, attains wealth through women, is rich yet free from sorrow, and is a hater of kinsmen while possessing great riches.
One born when the Moon is in Leo, Sagittarius, Aries, or Libra is wealthy, wise, impartial, and renowned;
one born in Capricorn lacks limbs, seeks wealth, is a coward, and is a friend of Brahmā (the Creator); one born in Gemini possesses the three kinds of happiness.

If the Moon is in the fifth house, there will be a virtuous son; if in the seventh, wealth through a wife; if in the tenth, the king [will be favorable]; and if in the eleventh, there will be fear of grief and other afflictions in the village.
If the Moon is in the fourth house, there will be suffering from the king, learned men, virtuous citizens, and from diseases such as leprosy and the like.
In the Avinīta-yuga, kings will be devoid of wealth, living as servants to their own intelligence;
those who live by mining minerals will be impoverished, and weavers will be terrified of the king’s knowledge. In their own [astrological] houses, they will be destitute.
Desire to fight, a poet, a hero, the three humors, life, vision, and disease;
light, knowledge, the wealthy, sacrifice, and indeed the king—these are the meanings of the root *ij* (to sacrifice) when preceded by *jñā* and others, as applied to Hari.
In the sixth house, through auspicious [planets], there is the desire for skill in leading royal armies;
in the seventh house (Jūka), kings, goldsmiths, and merchants [prosper] when conjoined with or aspected by the remaining [planets].
Those with two fathers, those with four arms, those with a banner on their head, those missing a limb, and those who rule their own lands—these are not kings.
Furthermore, at the beginning of the Kṛta age, there were virtuous men, while in the Kali age, people are likewise deceitful.
When the Moon is in Mṛgaśīrṣa, the girl will have a husband who is a king adorned with jewels;
when in Kumbha, she will have the remaining [qualities]; and when in the last asterism (Revatī), she will be known by the virtuous as one who knows humor and kingship.
The Moon is auspicious when it is aspected by or conjoined with planets situated in the eighth or seventh houses from the lord of the lagna;
likewise, it is so when it is conjoined with or aspected by a planet situated in a trine (triraśmi) or in a sign that is a friend to the lord of that trine.
The results for the twelfth division (dvādaśāṃśa) have been declared; now those for the ninth division (navāṃśa) are also being proclaimed:
one who is a protector, fond of killing, skilled in wrestling, or wealthy.

If Venus is situated in the portion of Mars, there is quarrel; one becomes a fool, a paramour of another's wife, a poet, happy, or a dancer, a thief, a knower [of secrets], or an artisan. (NarP 1.55.238)
In his own portion, however, the son of Hari is a friend with a small body, an ascetic devoted to greed,
prone to anger, a lord of treasures, a minister, or a king who is violent.
In the sub-period of Jupiter, one becomes a master of humor and knowledge, powerful, a counselor, and righteous;
however, having few children and being miserable, this occurs when Saturn is in the portion of a wicked woman.
In the case of the Bhānāri and other such aspects, one should declare the results to be exactly like that;
in a Vargottama, in its own sign, or in another sign, the results are auspicious in sequence.
If the lord of the navāṃśa is strong, it should be known as having a nourished middle and being light;
having obstructed the fruit of the sign-observation, it bestows the clear fruit of the navāṃśa.
When the Sun is situated in Aries in the ascendant, one becomes brave, stubborn, squint-eyed, and pitiless; in Leo, one is wealthy but suffers from cataracts and is blind at night.
If the Sun is in Capricorn, one is low-born and wicked; if situated in the first house, one has prominent eyes;
if in the second house, one possesses great wealth but is punished by the king and suffers from diseases of the mouth.

When Mercury is in the third house, one is courageous and victorious; when it is in the fourth house, one is distressed on earth, deprived of wealth and offspring; and when it is strong in the fifth house, one conquers enemies.

One conquered by women, addicted to gambling, with few sons and poor eyesight, yet possessing children, wealth, and happiness, and renowned for learning and valor, [is described] when Jupiter is in the tenth house.
If the Sun is in the eleventh house (lābha), one is wealthy and proud; if it is in the twelfth house (vyaya), one is indeed fallen.
If it is in the first house (mūka), one is mute; if in the second (adha), deaf; if in the third (preṣya), a servant; and if in the fourth (khāñca), one is wealthy. NarP_1,55.247 //

If Mars is in the tenth house, one will be wealthy and violent; if it is in the fourth house, there will be a virtuous nature and happiness; and if it is in the fifth house, there will be offspring in the form of daughters and laziness.

If the Sun is in the eighth house, the native will have weak digestion, sharp thighs, be envious, and suffer from diseases and afflictions; however, if it is in the second house, he will be endowed with friends and wealth.
In the reign of one who possesses the wealth of dharma and intellect, he shall become renowned for his wealth of intellect;
however, if the Moon is in the twelfth house, the wise declare the result to be meanness and physical deficiency.
If Mars is in the ascendant, one has a wounded body; if it is in the second house, one eats poor food;
if it is elsewhere, one is considered equal to the sun in conduct, though practicing both virtue and vice.
He is learned, wealthy, preeminent, and a wise counselor;
he knows the Dharma, possesses expansive virtues, and like the sun, he is profound and delights in what is to be known.

A learned man who is wretched, one whose eyes seek pleasure, one greedy for enemies, a base ascetic, one who is deceitful, covetous, and wicked—such a person is a burden upon his teacher. (NarP 1.55.253)
When Venus is situated in the mouth [the first house], one is full of longing; when situated in the waist [the seventh house], one is quarrelsome and eager for sexual union;
and when situated in the breasts [the second house], one is happy—provided Venus is elsewhere than with Jupiter.

When Saturn is situated in the ascendant, one is sighing, diseased, subject to lust, impure, afflicted by childhood ailments, and lazy; however, if it has gone to its own or exaltation sign in the ninth house, one becomes a king.
That wise lord of the village, possessing beautiful limbs like the sun elsewhere,
shall be full [in his results] when situated in its own sign or exaltation, and three-quarters [of that] when in its mula-trikona.
When a benefic planet is in its own sign or in a friendly sign, the result is eightfold;
in an enemy's sign, it is small; likewise, when it is in its sign of debilitation or set, there is an absence of results.
In the planets beginning with Khabharāka, one is respectively equal to one's family, superior to one's family, honored by kinsmen, wealthy, happy, an enjoyer of pleasures, or a king. (NarP 1,55.258)

The brother-in-law, friend, kinsman, dependent, leader of a host, and the king [are the significators] when the planets are situated in the signs beginning with Aries, respectively, as friends. (NarP 1.55.259)
When the Moon is situated in an odd asterism (viṣamarṣi) during its own horā, and in auspicious signs,
one becomes famous, highly industrious, exceedingly brilliant, wise, wealthy, and powerful.
When auspicious planets are situated in even signs during the Moon's horā,
a man will possess beauty, gentleness, good fortune, enjoyment, and intelligence.

A malefic planet situated in the solar hour (sūryahorā) is neutral in even signs, while in odd signs it is auspicious; however, planets in the lunar hour (bhāskaryā) do not bestow the aforementioned results.
The Moon situated in its own friend's third house makes a man handsome and virtuous;
likewise, when it is situated in the eleventh house, it makes him possess qualities and appearance equal to those [of his friends].
In Vyālāyudha, one becomes a four-footed beast; in Añja, a three-legged creature;
and in Tīkṣṇa, one becomes exceedingly cruel and a violator of the Guru’s bed.

He will be a thief, a consumer of others' wealth, a king with wealth and intellect yet impotent, a slayer of enemies, a laborer, one who lives as a slave, sinful, a doer of violence, and devoid of wisdom. (NarP 1.55.265)
In the twelve excellent portions beginning with Aries, as in the [twelve] signs,
one born is richly adorned with the strength of a wife, endowed with courage, and exceedingly bold.
A man who is lustful shall be born in the thirty-seventh part of the Khāya hell;
or he may be afflicted with disease through his own wife, or be an adulterer toward another's wife.
If Saturn is in its own [sign], one is miserable, possessed of attendants, and dirty;
yet he is happy in mind, wealthy, famous, diligent, radiant, and honored by the world.
If Jupiter is situated in the thirty-second part of the sign, one born in the Nīra-guhya division will be an enjoyer of pleasures,
endowed with intelligence, arts, poetry, craftsmanship, and eloquence, yet adorned with deceit.
If Mercury is in its own thirty-degree division, the native will be endowed with the courage to master the meaning of the scriptures;
however, he will be possessed of many calamities, unhappiness, fierce diseases, physical ailments, and loss of wealth.
Under his own [Jupiter], one will have graceful limbs and well-distributed faculties;
under Venus, one will be brave and steadfast, yet a killer of enemies, endowed with excellent qualities.

If the Moon and Sun occupy the third house while Mars and the other planets are situated in their Mūlatrikoṇa, own sign, or exaltation, the person will be pleasant to know and possess graceful limbs. // NarP_1,55.272 //
They become mutual agents, especially those situated in the sign of action;
there is auspicious birth when [the planets] are in Vargottama, in the station of Viśi, or in their own houses.
When the quadrants (kendras) and the houses known as the "causers" (kāraka-gṛhas) are not empty, Jupiter,
the lord of the birth sign, and the lord of the ascendant situated in the quadrants grant moderate happiness.
The Sun and Mars are situated in the last and middle quarters respectively during the entry [of a sign],
while Venus and Jupiter are likewise situated in the middle quarters.
The Moon and the Sun always bestow results at the end [of their periods], while Mercury is a giver of results throughout.
When the fifth or seventh house from the ascendant is conjoined with or aspected by a benefic lord, [it brings auspicious results].
Otherwise, there would be ownership of their wealth;
however, when the Sun is in the seventh house, there is fear, and Mars in the fifth house likewise destroys one's wife and sons.
If malefic planets occupy the eighth house from the Simānta yoga, or if Venus is situated between malefics,
yet is joined with or aspected by benefic planets, there will be death of the woman due to fire.
They say that for one whose birth occurs when the Moon and the Sun are together with a woman at the ascendant or elsewhere,
or when they are situated in the seventh house from each other, he will have [such a union].
Or if Venus and the Sun are deficient in their respective strengths,
or if they are situated in an angle at the time of rising or setting, or at the junction of day and night, there is the birth of a barren man's husband.
If the fifth house is not endowed with benefics, or if malefics occupy the twelfth, the ascendant, or the seventh house, and the Moon is situated in the fifth house waned at birth,
one will be childless and lack a wife.
If Saturn is in the seventh house with Venus and is aspected by it, the man becomes an adulterer;
if those two are together with the Moon and Venus, the man is born a libertine.
If Mars and Venus have set, a man’s wife or even his son may die;
however, if those two are aspected by benefics and possess full-bodied forms, they will bring prosperity to men and women.

If the Moon, Venus, and malefic planets occupy the eighth house, there will be the destruction of the lineage; if Mercury is in the third house and aspected by Saturn situated in a quadrant, one becomes an artisan.
If Venus is in the twelfth house in the portion of Saturn,
and both the Sun and the Moon are in their signs of debilitation or set, or are aspected by Saturn, [the native] is born of a maidservant.
If Saturn and Mars are in the sixth house, or are heliacally set, they cause diseases of the wind (vāta).
If the Moon is in Cancer or Aries and occupies a quadrant conjoined with a malefic, there is pain in the private parts.
If the Sun is in the seventh house from the Pāpāntara, one suffers from leprosy;
if the Moon is in the tenth house or set in the seventh, one is crippled; and if Saturn is in the fourth house, one is deformed.
When the Sun and the Moon are conjoined, one suffers from colic if they occupy the ninth or fifth houses from each other;
one becomes emaciated if they are in the eighth, sixth, second, or twelfth houses from each other; and when the Sun, Moon, Mars, and Saturn are situated in those same houses [from the ascendant].
Malign planets, when not aspected by benefics and situated in the third or eleventh houses, cause a man to suffer from the defect of squint through their flickering grasp.
If Jupiter is in the seventh house, there will be injury to the ears;
if Saturn is in the seventh house, it causes deformity of the teeth; or if Saturn is in the ascendant, one may suffer from diseases such as wind-disorders (vāta).
If Venus or Jupiter is situated in the fourth house, or if the ascendant is joined with Saturn,
or if Mars is in the seventh house and Mercury in the twelfth, or if the Moon is in the last (twelfth) house, the person is insane.
There is bondage by means of ashes due to sins located in the fourth, ninth, twelfth, and eleventh houses;
likewise, there is bondage by means of a snake or a chain through deceit, and by means of the aspects of the planets when they are aspected by malefics.
When Saturn is in the seventh house and is aspected by Mars, one suffers from epilepsy, foul speech, and consumption;
likewise when the Sun, Saturn, and Mars are situated in the seventh house and are aspected by benefics along with their orbs.
Servants are men who are classified as superior, middling, or inferior according to what was previously stated;
however, one should say that the fruit for those women who possess merit is appropriate to their own accumulation of merit.
All matters concerning her husband [are determined] by that; his death occurs when [the lord of the ascendant] dies.
The body is situated in the ascendant and the Moon; [this applies] when the day-lord has swallowed the rays [of the Moon].
If the Ascendant and the Moon are in even signs, the woman will be of a natural disposition;
she will be endowed with good character and ornaments if those two are aspected by benefics.
If those two [planets] are situated in the *ojas* (the odd houses), they are considered to have a human form and to be rich in virtue;
however, if those two are aspected by malefic planets and are devoid of virtues, they are sinful.
When Mars, Saturn, Jupiter, Mercury, and Venus are respectively in the sign of Mars, the woman is:
one who is wicked from childhood, a servant, virtuous, deceitful, or hasty. (NarP 1,55.298)
If those two [planets] are situated in the *ojas* houses, their appearance and character are considered auspicious;
however, if they are both aspected by malefics, they are sinful and devoid of virtues.
When Venus is in its own house, the woman born is harsh-spoken, yet reborn [to a higher state], virtuous, wise, and renowned;
when Mercury is there, she is even-tempered, impotent, chaste, virtuous, and fickle.
In the Dvandva-bha yoga, she is a wanton woman, a killer, rich in virtues, a lowly artisan, talkative, and unchaste; in the Siṃha yoga, she is passionate, wise, and unapproachable by men.
In Jupiter, she is rich in virtues, devoted to her husband, a knower of merit, wise, and virtuous; in Saturn, she is a slave, base, unchaste, wicked, and childless.
This result, following from the strength [of the planets], is determined by the trimśāṃśas joined with the Ascendant and the Moon;
when Venus and Saturn aspect each other in a degree, or if they are in a Navāṃśa belonging to Venus.
A woman, inflamed by the fire of passion, engages in sexual union with women;
a coward does so in an empty place, a gambler in a gambling den, and a eunuch in the army—not with one who is his equal.
If Mercury and the Sun are always in movable signs, one is constantly intent on foreign lands;
if the Sun is in that same sign during the period of intoxication (mada), one is a woman, a child, or a widow; and if Mars is there, it is likewise.
If Saturn, under an evil aspect, is in the seventh house, a maiden reaches old age;
if it is situated in the eighth house with fiery planets, she becomes a widow; if with Mars, she would become a remarried woman.
If a malefic planet, weak and situated in the eighth house, is abandoned by its lord, the woman will not be like her husband;
however, Venus and Mars, occupying each other's signs, cause the woman to be devoted to another.
When the cool-rayed moon is in the seventh house, she follows her husband's will;
but when Saturn, Mars, and the Moon are in the ascendant along with Venus, she is an unchaste woman.

If Mars is in an inauspicious aspect together with its mother, or if it is in a malefic Navamsha and heliacally set, there is a source of disease; however, if it is in a benefic planet's Navamsha, she is dear to her husband.
If the seventh house is in the sign or division of Mars, the husband of the woman is old and foolish;
if it is in that of Mars, he is lustful for women and irascible; if it is in that of Mercury, he is learned and skillful.

One born under Jupiter has conquered his senses; under Mercury, he is eloquent; under the Moon, he is lustful and gentle; under Venus, he is endowed with good fortune and is beloved; and under Saturn, he performs mild deeds.
If Venus and Jupiter are situated in the ascendant, she will be happy yet full of jealousy;
if Mercury and Jupiter are there, she will be skilled in the arts, happy, and endowed with virtues.
When the three benefics are situated in the ascendant, the woman born will be fortunate, skilled in the arts, and beautiful of limb; she will possess manifold happiness, wealth, and virtues.

If a malefic planet is in the eighth house and in the subdivision (aṃśa) of the lord of the eighth house, widowhood occurs for her at that age; however, if those [malefics] are in their own or exaltation signs, she herself dies.

If Saturn possesses middling strength while the Moon, Venus, and Mercury are devoid of strength, there will be few children for her; however, if these [planets] are situated in Cancer, Virgo, Libra, or Taurus, there will be daughters.

If the remaining planets are endowed with strength in a Lagna belonging to the sign of Ojas, the woman will be ill-formed; likewise, if Jupiter, Mars, Venus, and Mercury are strong in an even-sign Lagna, she will be so.

A woman renowned for her knowledge of many scriptures and a speaker of Brahman, though she may have committed sin, becomes a female ascetic when [Saturn] is in the ninth house from her. (NarP 1,55.317)
In matters of marriage, choosing a bridegroom, and making inquiries, one should consider all of this;
for those who observe the house of death, there may be danger due to the agitation of the bodily constituents by a powerful force.
In humans, a fever arising from many joints, accompanied by great pain in the limbs and body, and characterized by strength, frequent urination, and blood, is associated with death.
Thirst and hunger arise from the Sun and other planets situated in the eighth house;
there is death from enemies, weapons, travel, or foreign lands when the Sun and Mars are so placed.
For a man situated in his own *bandhu* house or in the *sthiti* house, if there is a planet rising in the sign of a mountain or fire, and it is afflicted by planets situated in the *bandhu*,
*asta*, or *karma* houses, or by those with weak strength, death occurs.

In the case of a woman, [the results] of the Moon and Mars occurring in the third house from the natal ascendant (svajana) are cold and heat; those of Saturn and Jupiter occurring in the third house from the natal ascendant are water and death; and when both [planets] arise in the tenth house, they are day and night.
If the Moon is situated within an inauspicious sign produced by weapons or fire and has entered the house of Mars, there is death;
furthermore, if the Moon is in Capricorn and Saturn is in Cancer, death occurs from dropsy.
If Mars is in the seventh house from the woman’s ascendant, death results from blood poisoning; if Saturn is there, it is caused by the fall of a horse or fire;
and if both malefic planets are situated in the fifth and ninth houses, it is due to imprisonment.

If Venus is in the seventh house, there will be imprisonment with shackles and fetters; if it is in the eighth house, death; if it is in the seventh house along with a malefic, suffering; if it is in the fourth house, gambling; and if the Sun is in Aries in the ascendant, [there will be loss].

In the fourth house, when Mars is aspected by a waning moon, there is a conflagration;
[the time of death] is determined by the numbers nine, zero, nine, and four, combined with the positions of the waning moon, Saturn, and the sun.
Then, with those very clubs held by the sons of Khaṅkāṅga stationed there, smoke should be produced from the bindings; through this, death shall occur.
If Mars, the Sun, and Jupiter are situated in the houses of kinsmen, enemies, or the eighth house, one suffers from weapons, fire, or kings;
if Saturn and Venus are situated in their own, the fourth, or the tenth house, there is injury to the head, the anus, and the limbs.
If Mars is in the fourth house from the ascendant, there is death by a vehicle accident; or if Mars is set and conjoined with the waning moon, death occurs due to the collapse of a machine.

Death occurs when Mars, Saturn, and the Moon are situated in Libra, Aries, and the sign of Saturn (Aquarius) respectively, and the waning Moon, the Sun, and Mars are located in the tenth, seventh, and fourth houses from the lord of the day.
O Aṅgiras, when Venus is not visible, the moon is waning, and Saturn is situated in the eighth house,
death occurs from secret diseases, worms, weapons, fire, or wood.

If the Sun is in the sixth house, Saturn is deceased, the Moon is waning, and Mars is not conjoined with the Earth (the Ascendant), and if the lords of the Ascendant and the fifth house set while afflicted by Saturn, the Sun, Mars, and the Moon; NarP_1,55.333 //
If there is a violent fall from a mountain peak, death will occur;
if the difference between the ascendant and the moon is twenty-four degrees, its lord or the lord of the eighth house will cause death.
One who is strong through his own qualities should not act as a storehouse for both;
death occurs when there is a similarity between the lord of the ascendant and the lord of the navāṃśa, due to yogas, aspects, and so forth.
The portion of the moon that has risen is equal [to the result] when doubled for one's own desired [object];
however, if it is aspected by a benefic, it is tripled; other matters should be inferred by one's own intelligence.
One should contemplate the body of the embodied being as it is described: as fire, water, earth, ashes, moisture, dryness, and serpents, all existing within death. ||| NarP_1,55.337 |||
Jupiter, the Moon, and Venus, as well as the Sun, Mars, Saturn, and Mercury,
and the deity of the ancestors (Yama), when situated in the eighth house, cause one to become a hell-being.
The Sun, Moon, Mars, Mercury, Jupiter, Venus, and Saturn are superior, middling, and inferior according to their strength;
one situated in its exaltation is followed by the *sāṃdana* yoga, which is the aspect of six, eight, and twelve signs.
If Jupiter is situated in the seventh house, or is placed in the sixth,
tenth, or eighth houses, yet is in its exaltation sign in the first or twelfth house within a benefic division, liberation occurs due to strength from other factors.
One should declare birth from the ascendant (lagna) when it is known; however, one should declare the state of being a tree from the ascendant.
Birth from a tree should be predicted from the first or second half of the ascendant, or from a benefic planet.
In the trikoṇa (trine) of the ascendant, the parts of the alternatives are equal by means of the one-fourth and one-third portions;
during the summer solstice, when the sun is in the opposite sign from the sun's position at the start of the season, [the days] are delightful.
If this [lunar day] is obscured by the Moon, Mercury, or Jupiter, it is otherwise by Venus, Mars, or Saturn;
through the aspects and so forth, the previous month and lunar day are determined there by proportion.
The time [of birth] is determined by the degrees of retrograde birth, designated as night or day; the ascendant is either the trine, the exaltation, the friend, or the neutral sign. (NarP 1.55.344)
To the extent that the moon is deficient from the ascendant (lagna), to that same extent it is deficient from the moon at birth;
[this applies when] the signs Taurus, Leo, Virgo, and Libra are joined with Aries and Gemini, while Capricorn and Aquarius are joined with Sagittarius and Pisces.
In the domains of ten, eighteen, and seven, the remaining [planets] are multiplied by zero;
Jīva, Bhauma, Kavi, and Vijña are like Rāghava, Ādya, Āya, and Rejña.
The rule for the [mean] positions is constant; likewise, the day-counts (dhargaṇa) are determined by the power of the planets.
Multiply the [day-count] by seven and divide by the [number of] lunar mansions (bhā); the remainder is the asterism (ṛkṣa), according to the addition or subtraction of nine.
When doubled, they become the even months; when divided by eight, they become the fortnights and lunar days.
When multiplied by seven, they become the deficient nights and asterisms; when multiplied by five, they become the *iṅga*-parts and the *iṣṭa*-hours.
A man holding an axe, dark-complexioned and with red eyes, is capable of protecting her;
she has been seen and comforted by him, wearing red garments and having the form of a water-pot.
For Kapila was cruel, with blinded vision, wearing red garments, and having violated his vows;
he was afflicted by hunger and thirst, clad in a tattered cloth, with hair that was shorn and curled.
Soiled, his face pale from hunger and exhaustion, he was skillful in tasks such as agriculture;
with a body like that of a wild beast, his throat parched from fear of the *sarabha*, his inner being was deeply agitated.
A virtuous woman, pure and beautiful, childless yet with hands raised high;
a man with the face of Garuḍa, clad in armor and bearing a bow, shall sport in the garden.
He is the preeminent master of dance and other arts, like Varuṇa; he wields a bow rich with many jewels;
he has the face of an elephant and the neck of a lion; he has the face of a boar; and he is the lord of the forest and the wielder of arrows.

One who is harsh as a serpent at the head, flat-faced, and covered, crying out toward a branch of the *pālāśa* tree in the forest, is like one traveling by boat upon the water for the sake of wealth. (NarP 1.55.354)
A man, having seized a jackal and a vulture, cries out upon a silk-cotton tree; armed with a bow and wearing a black antelope skin, he is distressed by the loud roar of a lion.
Phalāmiṣaghna, Kūrjīna, Bhallāsya, Kapiceṣṭita, Puṣpapūrṇacchaṭā, Kanyāvidyellā, and Malināmbara. (NarP 1.55.356)
The archer, the destroyer of expenditure, the dark one, the painter, Rāma, and Śonara;
[he was seen] in the abode of the Asuras by Gaurī, Dhautāṃśukā, Sūcī, Kumbhī, and Dṛṣṭi.

A man who is full of pride and conceit, who considers himself a vessel for the removal of sins, who is afflicted by hunger and thirst, and who is greedy for a water-pot while attending to his wife and children; NarP_1,55.358 //
A bowman moving within the forest, clad in golden armor and pursuing deer;
a woman crying out as she walks upon the ocean, accompanied by various hissing white serpents.
With limbs covered by the desire for pleasure, his body having the form of a tortoise,
with a tortoise-like face, he was a lion in Malaya who terrified dogs, jackals, and deer.
Vāsya, Śvakāya, Dhānuṣka, Raṅkṣa, Tāpasa, Yajñiya;
Caṃpakābhāsana, Madhya, Siṃdhu, and Atrevivardhinī.
In the tortoise posture, he was the color of a campaka flower, carrying a staff, and wearing silk garments;
then there was the supreme one with a vulture’s face, who longed for oil and liquor as food.
Dagdhānastha, Lohadhara, Sabhūṣa, Bhāñjaka, Kaccara, Bhāṇḍī, Romaśvā, Śyāma, Kirīṭin, and Phalayantradhṛk.
Adorned with various ornaments made of many jewels, she stood upon the ship;
then Campakānanā, together with her companions, approached the shore of the vessel.
Enveloped by snakes in a pit, naked, weeping, and tormented by thieves and fire—
such are the thirty-six parts of action that have been declared in sequence.
O best of sages, this Jātaka has been declared in brief;
now understand the Saṃhitā section, which is useful for the practical affairs of the world.
Thus ends the fifty-fifth chapter, titled "The Description of Birth," in the Bṛhad-upākhyāna of the second quarter of the first part of the glorious Nāradīya Purāṇa.
Sanandana said:
"In due order, during the months beginning with Caitra, the transits [of the sun] are considered to occur in the signs beginning with Aries."
The day of the week on which the first day of the bright fortnight of Caitra falls is known as the King.
When the Sun enters Aries, he becomes a commander of armies; in Cancer, he becomes a lord of grain.
The Sun is middling when rising with the planets, and the Moon is excellent.
Mars is not desired; Mercury, Jupiter, and Venus bring great auspiciousness; whereas Saturn is to be declared as inferior—having understood the relative strength and weakness of these [planets].
If a staff-shaped, headless trunk, crow-shaped,
or stake-shaped form appears within the orb of the sun, there will be disease, delusion, thieves, and the loss of wealth.
With sounds resembling umbrellas, banners, and flags,
and with smoky, ash-colored masses accompanied by sparks moving across the circle of the sky, there was the destruction of the world.
